summary: Department of Forests and Waters built a 60 ft steel tower on Penobscot Knob in 1925; burned and replaced in 1941; manned into 1962.

events.note: Site developed as a replacement for the Glen Summit station.
60 ft steel forest fire observation tower with glass-enclosed top erected by the Department of Forests and Waters on Penobscot Knob.
Margery Weyhenmeyer of Nuangola appointed fire warden in charge of the tower.
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description says the summit is occupied by the Penobscot Forest Lookout Tower.
Dirt road built by forest fire wardens, about three-quarters of a mile from the concrete road to the tower.
Tower used as an air defense lookout; observers assigned to spot plane movements over 32 square miles.
Tower burned about a week before the report dated October 11, 1941; the article calls it a mysterious burning.
Structure replaced hastily during the week after the fire.
John Hasselberger in charge of the Mountain Top fire tower.
Penobscot Tower operated by Austin Hauser.
Penobscot and other fire towers manned round the clock during a dry spell; usually manned only in April, May, October and November.

evidence.supports: WNEP-TV analog transmitter tower collapsed in December 2007 due to severe ice, winds and snow
evidence.quote: WNEP-TV's transmission tower broadcasting the analog signal on channel 16 collapsed on December 16, 2007, [ 2 ] due to severe ice, winds, and snow at the transmitter location on Penobscot Knob.

evidence.supports: Summit is known as Penobscot Knob on the highest peak of the Wyoming Mountain
evidence.quote: OF THE WYOMING MOUNTAIN, KNOWN AS PENOBSCOT KNOB

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources call the summit Penobscot Knob, Wilkes-Barre Mountain and Wyoming Mountain. The 1929 station description names Penobscot Knob as the peak of the Wyoming Mountain, so the story uses Penobscot Knob.

notes_for_editor: Fire tower's fate after 1962 is not in any source found; Wikipedia covers only the summit transmitters. Story says nothing about the tower's present condition beyond that. Elevation (2,100 ft) is in the text, not a facts key. The 1941 replacement is described as hasty with no height given. Grokipedia copy and Google Books blurb were not read.
